about: Body rows for tools/cut-batch.mjs (docs/CUT-BATCH.md). One row per body; every per-body number lives here, never in the tool. `source` is relative to --sources (or $CUT_SOURCES). Bodies are confidential: the sources are never committed, only these rows.

bodies.name: demon-106
bodies.blocked: one skinned mesh (Steel, material Demon_MAT, 9,340 vertices, no hair material) whose shell is not closed where the cut planes pass: 756 open source edges, and the section loops at the shoulder planes (x = +-0.261) and the crotch plane (x = 0, hip_split) do not close, so 586 cap-loop edges stay open (84 root, 132 torso, 87 + 45 arms, 106 + 106 legs). The thigh pieces also get 11 flipped-winding edges each on the crotch plane (orientation) and 1 root vertex lands 0.0001 m on the wrong side of the hip_right plane (planes). A sweep of neck_frac {0.5, 0.2, 0.8} x waist_frac {1, 0.8, 0.6} x shoulder_frac {0, 0.1, 0.2} x hip_frac {0, 0.1, 0.2} (81 cuts), home_min_weight {0.1, 0.35, 0.5} and crotch_planes false gave no PASS (crotch_planes false leaves leg_left with no triangles). The mesh is one primitive with one material, so there is no sub-mesh to drop or hand to the head. Needs a closed (or hand-capped) shell at the shoulders and between the legs in the source.

bodies.name: parasite-106
bodies.note: V3 boss Parasite (The Titan's Envoy), Frankendom-v3 PR 226 head 017f932 (src/assets/parasite-106.glb, 2,009,476 bytes, sha256 e3014ea7...ee1f, 10,930 tris, 106 joints, stem parasite; confidential source, not committed). OpenTrident Dev capped 66 open edges (throat ring + 2 jaw holes) in the source; all 8 checks pass with no bypass. The source keeps native boundary edges that the cut leaves alone: OpenTrident counted 410 (eye loops); the validator counts 438 on the source surface and 442 on the pieces (head 296, upper torso 50, root 38, legs 29 + 29), none introduced by a cut and none crossing a cut plane. Capping them would cover the eyeballs. Default planes, no hair material; 7 pieces (root, upper_torso, head, arm_left, arm_right, leg_left, leg_right) + 12 caps; cut GLB 2,848,452 bytes, 1,943,703 gzipped.

bodies.name: big-vegas-106
bodies.blocked: V3 boss Big Vegas (The King), Frankendom-v3 PR 229 head 7327835 (src/assets/big-vegas-106.glb, 678,832 bytes, one skinned mesh Steel 4,584 vertices plus eyes, brows and mouth). With the hip bisector fixed (parallel thighs: the midline plane) the cut still fails 3 of 8 checks: the belly and the Hips-skinned pants run across the midline between the legs (the legs never reach it: left and right inner thigh at x = +-0.10 m, crotch underside at y = 0.76 m), so mesh sits under both plain hip planes and the cut leaves 14 over-used edges and 32 flipped-winding edges in the two leg pieces, cap_shoulder_left_arm with 2 of 50 triangles wound against their normals and 1 over-used edge in piece_upper_torso. Turning the hip planes to a crotch apex at the pants underside instead moves the failure into piece_root (71 flipped edges, 2 root caps inward) because the turned planes climb to the flanks at y = 1.06. A wall cap on the midline, or a crotch apex that does not tilt the planes into the flanks, is the open tool work.
bodies.note: hip_split noise fix: tools/cut-units.mjs HIP_SPLIT_PARALLEL; the 8 shipped cut rows regenerate byte-identical

bodies.name: warrior-65
bodies.blocked: the skin shell EXO_BrowsLashes (material Exo_MAT, 9,352 vertices, the body under the Steel suit) is open geometry: 195 section chains at the cut planes do not close, so 696 cap-loop edges stay open (166 root, 234 torso, 89 + 89 arms, 58 + 58 legs). Dropping that mesh from the cut gives 0 introduced open edges (measured on the VPS), but it holds the visible face, hands and neck skin, so it cannot be dropped. Needs a closed (or hand-capped) skin shell in the source; a cut tool bridge across the hidden gaps would draw caps over geometry that is not there.

bodies.name: veteran-65
bodies.blocked: the body mesh CreatureBody (47,360 vertices) is a non-manifold sculpt: the source already has 2,003 open and 1,765 over-used edges and 49 flipped-winding edges (cut-validate --self), six skinned meshes overlap each other, and the section loops through them are tangled (117 loops, 38 holes, 44 forced ears, 50 inward cap triangles). The cut then introduces open edges (watertight: 6 root, 14 torso, 12 head, 2+2 legs, 15 + 2 + 3 + 2 over-used) and 1,054 flipped-winding edges in piece_root (orientation). The cut is geometrically complete (conservation, weights, bone side, planes, caps all PASS). Needs a cleaned body mesh (merge the overlapping shells, fix the non-manifold edges) before the caps can close.

bodies.name: vagrant-106
bodies.blocked: six overlapping skinned garment meshes on one skin (Backpack, Feet boots, Legs trousers, Protection vest, Torso jacket, Vagrant body; 28,640 vertices, 1,639 open source edges: hems, openings and layers that are not closed shells), so every cut plane passes through several unclosed layers: 589 open edges at the cuts, 7 of 7 pieces with open edges introduced by the cut (187 root, 76 torso, 16 + 16 arms, 115 + 177 legs, plus 1 over-used edge on leg_left), and winding that disagrees with the normals on 2 of 161 triangles of cap_shoulder_left_arm and 3 of 166 of cap_hip_left_leg (caps). Orientation, weights, bone_side, conservation and planes pass. A sweep of neck_frac {0.5, 0.2, 0.8} x waist_frac {1, 0.8, 0.6} x shoulder_frac {0, 0.1, 0.2} x hip_frac {0, 0.1, 0.2} (81 cuts) gave no PASS. Needs the garments merged into one closed (or hand-capped) shell in the source.
bodies.note: Armagedom player Vagrant (Web/public/assets/appearances/vagrant-106.glb): 19-joint Mixamo skeleton, so Spine1 is a node outside the skin and the toes are synthesised from the Foot (rig map mixamo-19). hair_materials is empty: the default hair pattern (hair|lash|brow) matches 'browser' in every material name (Backpack browser, Torso jacket browser, ...), which sent every triangle to piece_head; the Vagrant has no hair mesh. The machete (WeaponDrawn_1, WeaponDrawn_2) is unskinned and not cut

bodies.name: hale-pitborn
bodies.blocked: nine skinned meshes on eight 65-joint skins, layered over one another (Photo, PhotoEyes, PhotoTeeth, Bone, Pitborn_L3_Armour, OriginalHead_Steel, OriginalHead_Wrap, Fitted joint sleeves, Recovered donor lower neck; 54,628 vertices, 2,769 open source edges): 2,371 open edges at the cuts, 9 pieces with open or over-used edges introduced by the cut (493 open edges on upper_torso and 400 on head at the neck plane, over-used edges on the root, both arms, both legs) and 5 pieces with flipped winding (142 root, 664 torso, 92 head, 194 + 366 arms). Caps, weights, bone_side, conservation and planes pass. A sweep of neck_frac {0.5, 0.2, 0.8} x waist_frac {1, 0.8, 0.6} x shoulder_frac {0, 0.2} (18 cuts), home_min_weight 0.5 and crotch_planes false gave no PASS (crotch_planes false leaves a region with no triangles). Needs the armour, sleeves and head layers merged into one closed (or hand-capped) shell at the neck, shoulders and hips in the source.
